explanation: Backtrack over candidate indices in nondecreasing order. Reusing the current index permits repeated values; never moving backward prevents duplicate combinations.
timeComplexity: O(c^(d+1) + output size) upper bound for c candidates and d = target / smallest candidate. The recursion depth is at most d=floor(target/min(candidates)); each level tries c candidates. Copying successful paths contributes the total output length.
spaceComplexity: O(d) recursion and current-path space, excluding output. The active path and recursion stack each have at most d entries; saved solutions are output space.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The path uses candidate indices in nondecreasing order, so every multiset of chosen candidates has one recursion order. Reusing the same index permits repeated copies. Each call subtracts a positive candidate, and reaching remainder zero records exactly a target-sum combination; every valid multiset follows one such branch.
walkthrough: For candidates [3,4,7] and target 10, choosing 3,3,4 completes one branch. Choosing 3,7 completes another. No other candidate multiset totals 10, so return [[3,3,4],[3,7]].
edgeCases: Candidates are positive and distinct, so recursive remainders strictly decrease.
The public target is at least 1; zero remainder is the successful internal base case.
Candidates larger than the remaining target are skipped.
A candidate may be reused; changing selection order does not create a new combination.
